timing: Editorial cue timings retained from the original animation; English narration is a translation and is not aligned to a recorded voice.

cues.narration: All of this is possible because of light.
cues.visual: A light wave and a γ symbol appear.

cues.narration: Light consists of photons, which are elementary particles.
cues.visual: The γ symbol is highlighted inside a large particle tile.

cues.narration: But there are many other elementary particles, each with different properties.
cues.visual: The photon tile moves into the Standard Model table as the other 16 tiles appear; particle families are highlighted.

cues.narration: Different particles can provide different kinds of information about the universe.
cues.visual: The full table remains visible while the photon and three neutrino tiles stand out.

cues.narration: This leads to the central idea of neutrino astronomy:
cues.visual: The three neutrino tiles move from their table positions to the foreground.

cues.narration: detecting neutrinos from some of the most energetic events in the universe.
cues.visual: A schematic cosmic source emits a muon neutrino, which produces a muon in ice and lights nearby DOMs.
